chapter: After high school: riverfront and tailoring
title: Meeting Lewis Silvers and the meaning of the zoot suit
summary: A salesman named Warren brought him to Silvers' shop; Tex explains the zoot suit style tied to Cab Calloway and Count Basie.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So, well, how did you meet Lewis, Lewis Silver? That was, I don't think you really...

Well, Warren, who was a salesman for him who lived in my neighborhood, Warren brought me down there because I wanted to get me a Zoot Suit. That was my first. So, that's how I got a chance to meet Mr. Silver's because after buying a Zoot Suit, then I bought a couple of other pair of pants down there and bought another suit and whatnot. And the man took a liking to me. He said, hey son, would you like to work? I quit the riverfront and I started selling clothes for him.
Oh, okay. So, you were working on the river. Oh, okay. I'm sure...
Working on the river and selling clothes all at the same time.
So, tell us what a Zoot Suit is for somebody who doesn't know what a Zoot Suit is.

Well, now, let me tell you what a Zoot Suit is. In 1939, Clark Gable came out with Gone with the Wind and everybody's wearing these long coats. Kev Calloway got on radio, I mean on the movies, and he started with his hidey hole thing with the big white, big apple hat and with the Zoot Suit and it started taking off. The image factor. And then Count Basie came up with going to Chicago with his big time band. I wanted to go to Chicago. I finally got to Chicago, but before I got to Chicago, I wanted to make sure that I had me a big apple hat and I wanted to have me a Zoot Suit like everybody else.
Was that about why you bought the Zoot Suit?
